rv.q: Part Two finds its footing and doesn’t take one wrong step: the humour working brilliantly in occasional flecks, the drama leading with emotion, thought and the everyday tragedy of marital disappointment.
That playwright Nina Raine, director Jeremy Herrin and a committed and well-integrated cast have done so brilliantly is little short of miraculous.
This vivid and emotional adaptation is definitely a theatrical highlight of the year so far, and further evidence that bringing more books to the stage is the way forward.

No, not The Archers , but Nina Raine’s daring, dramatic distillation of Middlemarch , George Eliot’s 1871 mighty, moving masterpiece chronicling the interconnected lives of the residents of a country town.
What makes the whole entirely compelling is its fluidity and grace and the sheer calibre of the acting.
Jeremy Herrin's fleet, sparely designed production impresses, as secrets spill and paths intersect.
